title: Run King! RUN!!!: Choose the Mating Piece
summary: Offer the queen so the king must choose between queen mate on h7 and bishop mate on the same square.

nodes.question: Which piece should finish the attack on h7?
nodes.explanation: Qf5+ checks Kg6 and offers the queen to the king. Kxf5 permits Bh7 mate; declining with Kg7 or Kh6 leaves Qh7 mate instead. Black’s bishop on f6 blocks a flight square for its own king.

branches.title: Source finish: the king takes the queen
commentary: Begin in the later full-board diagram. The earlier knight sacrifice and king chase are context; no spare pawn, rook or bishop is removed from this reconstruction.
Qf5+ offers the queen with check along the f5–g6 diagonal. The king has three legal choices, and every one leads to mate on h7.
Kxf5 accepts the queen with the king. Black’s bishop stays on f6, occupying a square the king would otherwise need when the bishop checks.
Bh7# checks f5 along h7–g6–f5. Kg3 covers f4/g4, h4 controls g5, and Black’s e5 pawn, Re6 and Bf6 block three more flights. The bishop’s checking diagonal also covers e4 and g6.
branches.explanation: Bh7# checks f5 along h7–g6–f5. Kg3 covers f4/g4, h4 controls g5, and Black’s e5 pawn, Re6 and Bf6 block three more flights. The bishop’s checking diagonal also covers e4 and g6.

branches.title: Independent defense: retreat to g7
commentary: The king can decline the queen. Check that retreat instead of assuming the queen must be taken.
Qf5+ starts the same offer. The saved certificate checks every legal king reply.
Kg7 retreats up the g-file. Black avoids the immediate bishop mate on f5 but leaves h7 available to the queen.
Qh7# checks along the seventh rank. Bg8 protects h7; Qh7 covers h8, h6, g6 and f7, while Rf8 occupies f8. Black cannot capture the protected queen or block the adjacent queen check.

branches.title: Independent defense: retreat to h6
commentary: The other legal refusal moves toward the board’s edge.
Qf5+ checks while keeping the queen ready to switch to h7.
Kh6 avoids the capture on f5, but the king’s edge position gives the queen a direct mating square.
Qh7# checks down the h-file. Bg8 protects the queen, Qh7 closes g7/g6/h5, and White’s h4 pawn controls g5. The king cannot capture on h7.

exercises.prompt: Which black piece captures the queen in the source?
exercises.answer: The king captures with Kxf5. The bishop remains on f6, occupying an escape square for its own king.
No. Kg7 and Kh6 are legal. Both allow Qh7 mate, while Kxf5 allows Bh7 mate.
